acceptance_condition: Either a proved improvement N(H) = O(H^{rho'}) with rho' < ln3/ln11, or a proved lower bound N(H) >= c*H^beta for some beta > 0 that brackets the exponent, or a rigorous statement that branching-3 with factor exactly 11 occurs along a positive-density set of branches (making rho sharp for this method).
rationale: The upper bound treats each fast subtree as a worst-case 3-ary tree with minimal factor 11; both assumptions are generically far from tight, so the exponent 0.4582 is an artifact of the method. The most informative next mathematical step is quantifying typical branching and typical factor inside one fast subtree.
text: Is the exponent rho = ln3/ln11 = 0.4582 improvable toward the true growth rate of N(H)? Specifically: inside subtree(u_j), bound how often vertices have the full 3 distinct children versus equal-coordinate coincidences, and how the per-edge factor (>= 11, typically much larger) distributes; combine with the lower-bound thread to decide whether N(H) = Theta(H^alpha) for some alpha or whether the true growth is polylogarithmic-times-subpower.
